e7_champion: Myocardial infarction with normal coronary arteries
e7_s3: Myocardial infarction with normal coronary arteries
e7_s4_rationale: The patient presented with chest pain and initial ECG changes (ST-segment elevation) consistent with myocardial infarction, but coronary angiography revealed normal coronary arteries without stenosis, which is characteristic of myocardial infarction with normal coronary arteries.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Acute coronary syndrome
e7_s4_rejected.why: While the patient presented with symptoms and ECG changes consistent with acute coronary syndrome, the normal coronary arteries on angiography make this less likely.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Takotsubo cardiomyopathy
e7_s4_rejected.why: Although the patient had right ventricular dilatation, the initial ECG changes and the lack of a clear stressor make this diagnosis less likely.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Pulmonary embolism
e7_s4_rejected.why: The patient's symptoms and diagnostic findings, such as the ECG changes and normal oxygen saturation, do not strongly support pulmonary embolism.

e7_s4_rejected.label: Spontaneous coronary artery dissection
e7_s4_rejected.why: The coronary angiography showed normal coronary arteries, which does not support the diagnosis of spontaneous coronary artery dissection.
